input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Clause 28.1 selects Singapore law with exclusive Singapore courts, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and amounts to an exclusive foreign venue — walk-away territory under the rule. It also directly conflicts with 28.2, which already gives exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. The minimal fix is to change only the jurisdiction and forum words in 28.1 to New York law and New York County courts, aligning with 28.2 and reaching the preferred position; the rest of the sentence and the 28.3 escalation process are unchanged and acceptable.

ops.oldText: governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
ops.newText: governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law and forum in 28.1 from Singapore to New York law and the courts of New York County, which is our standard position and also removes the direct conflict with the exclusive New York venue already agreed in 28.2. If helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales (with the courts of London) as an alternative.
proposal.summary: Replace Singapore law/courts in 28.1 with New York law and New York County courts.
